# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]

I need to figure out what these gestures mean. Mute can read the manual but can't speak, so they're using gestures to communicate something to me. Let me think about what I can share back.

I can see: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [green], WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

Mute sent three gesture pairs to me: [👍 ✌], [✌ 🖐], [🖐 👍]. This looks like it could be asking me about specific things - possibly pairing symbols with wire positions or asking me to confirm colors using a code. Since I don't have an established code yet, I should first report what I see in plain terms via speech to Mute and Blind, since both can hear me. This establishes a baseline so Mute (who has the manual) can guide us, and Blind (who can act) knows what's on the display.

I'll speak plainly since that reaches both Mute and Blind, giving them my raw observations. I'll hold off on interpreting the unclear gesture code until I understand it better.

```
speak(text="I see: display shows 0, light is green, wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is red")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute is repeating the same gesture [👍 ✌] to me again. Since Mute can't speak and can't see, they must be trying to establish a signal code with me using gestures alone. This repetition suggests it's important - perhaps they're asking me to confirm something, or establishing a symbol meaning.

Since I already told them what I see via speech (which only Blind could hear too, not Mute... wait, Mute can't hear either). Let me reconsider: Mute cannot hear. So my speech last turn reached only Blind, not Mute. Mute only receives gestures from me.

So Mute has been gesturing to me, but doesn't know I received it, and can't receive my speech. I need to gesture back to Mute to communicate. I should acknowledge receipt and try to convey the wire colors through gestures since that's the only channel to Mute.

Let me establish a simple mapping: I'll gesture to Mute using distinct symbols for each color I see, thumbs up as acknowledgment first, then try to convey wire info via gestures since that's our only shared channel.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals this turn. I acknowledged Mute's gesture with a thumbs up and a peace sign, but I don't know if that meant anything to them. I need to actually establish communication of the bomb's details to Mute via gestures, since that's our only channel.

Let me think about a strategy: I should encode the wire colors and positions using gestures. I could use a system where I point to establish position, then use a symbol for color. Since Mute repeated [👍 ✌] three times with variations before, they might be trying to ask me something specific - possibly "what color is wire 1" or similar, using a gesture-based query system they've set up based on their manual instructions.

Since I don't know their code, I should proactively establish my own simple, clear system: gesture numbers using finger-count-like symbols, then colors. Let me try using ☝ ✌ 🤟 for wire 1, 2, 3, and distinct symbols for colors (yellow, green, red).

I'll define: ☝=wire1, ✌=wire2, 🤟=wire3, then follow with a color symbol. Let me pick: 👍=green, ✋=yellow, ✊=red (arbitrary but consistent).

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still no arrivals. My gestures went out but I have no confirmation Mute understood the code I invented, since Mute can't respond to me directly with anything I'd understand except gestures - and Mute can gesture back? Wait, checking the rules: Mute can gesture too (gestures are hand-based, not speech). Actually the rules say Mute "cannot speak" but gestures are separate from speech. Let me reconsider - Mute has been gesturing to me already, so Mute CAN gesture. But my gestures to Mute - does Mute receive gestures? Mute "cannot see" wasn't stated as a limitation for Mute - only Deaf cannot hear/touch, Mute cannot speak/touch, Blind cannot see.

So Mute CAN see gestures (no restriction stated against it) and CAN gesture. Good - that confirms gesture channel works both ways between us.

I should continue sending my color/wire mapping and also send the light and display info. Let me also include the display and light status.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👐", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing back. Let me reconsider the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf - every round. So within a round, Mute speaks/gestures first, then Blind, then I (Deaf) go last. What I send lands on whoever comes after me "in that same round" - but I'm last, so my messages would go to next round's Mute and Blind? Wait, re-reading: "Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round."

Since I'm last (Deaf goes third), nobody comes after me in the same round. So my gestures/speech land... at the start of the next round for whoever can perceive them. That explains why Mute's gestures arrive to me, and my gestures to Mute should arrive to Mute at the start of next round too.

But I've sent gestures for 4 turns now with no response from Mute via gestures back to me. Maybe Mute doesn't need to respond, or maybe Mute's messages are going to Blind only now, or maybe Mute already has what they need and is now trying to instruct Blind directly (since Mute goes before Blind in the same round, Mute can talk to Blind directly).

Actually that makes sense! Mute reads the manual and speaks to Blind (who can hear) to guide the action. Mute may no longer need me. My job might be done - I already told them the colors. Let me just keep sending the info in case it's needed, and wait otherwise.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute sent the same [👍 ✌] gesture again (this is the 4th time total, but with gaps). This seems to be a fixed message they keep repeating, not adapting to what I send. Perhaps Mute doesn't have a way to know I've been sending info back, or this gesture has a specific fixed meaning tied to the manual instructions that doesn't change based on my responses.

Let me think about this differently. Maybe [👍 ✌] is Mute's way of asking "wire 2" or confirming something about position 2, using their own numbering system (✌ = 2, similar to how I used it). 👍 could mean "confirm/check" or "is it green" (matching my own convention accidentally).

Given wire 2 is green - if Mute is asking "is wire 2 green?" via 👍(yes/check) ✌(2), I should respond confirming. Let me answer with a thumbs up to confirm wire 2 is indeed green, using consistent gesture logic.

Actually, better: let me try answering their exact query pattern back - if they're asking about wire 2, I'll gesture the color of wire 2.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No response again. Let me reconsider — maybe Mute's repeated gesture [👍 ✌] isn't a query at all, but is a fixed protocol/handshake message unrelated to needing my input, or perhaps Mute has already learned enough and is now coordinating with Blind (who hears Mute) to defuse the bomb, and my gestures aren't reaching Mute effectively, or Mute simply isn't checking for gestures from me since they already have their manual instructions and are waiting for Blind's action confirmation.

Given the situation is static (same board every turn) and Mute's message hasn't changed to acknowledge my new information, I should keep transmitting the wire/light/display data clearly and consistently in case it's needed, while also trying a different simpler encoding in case my color-coding wasn't understood.

Let me simplify: just show the wire colors one at a time using distinct unique gestures I haven't reused for other purposes, to avoid ambiguity with my earlier possibly-misread "reply" gesture.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤲", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊]

Now Mute sent something different: [👍 ✊]. Previously it was [👍 ✌] repeated. Now the second symbol changed from ✌ to ✊. In my encoding, ✊ = red (wire 3's color), and ✌ = wire 2 position. This shift could mean Mute is now asking about a different wire, or reacting to my red=✊ signal I sent.

Wait, actually — maybe Mute is mirroring back symbols I sent, confirming receipt! I sent 🤟+✊ for wire 3 = red. If Mute is acknowledging with 👍(confirm) + ✊(the red symbol), that suggests they received my color code for red and are confirming it.

Let me confirm this hypothesis by responding with an acknowledgment gesture, and continue sending the remaining wire info to complete the picture, in case Mute is now working through each one systematically.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
wait()
```
